title: Planning ahead
description: Earlier activations encode future outputs and may shape intervening text.

claims.heading: Claude 3.5 Haiku plans rhyme endings before writing the line
A single hidden state can predict tokens several positions ahead
Models compute features for later tokens beyond immediate next-token prediction
Rhyme planning appears in open models, but its reach is contested
Internal look-ahead extends to reasoning, chess and Sokoban
Planning can be shallow or incidental

related_findings.title: Early states reveal properties of upcoming responses
related_findings.summary: Hidden states at the prompt and early in generation reveal properties of upcoming responses: length, when harmful content begins, and the spread of numeric outputs. These measurements do not establish prediction of exact future tokens, and estimated ranges contain the outputs less often under distribution shift.

examples.headline: Graph-based regression predicts remaining output length from hidden states, outperforming TRAIL’s length predictions across three models.
A Qwen3-8B probe predicts whether harmful content begins within 16 tokens.
Quantile probes estimate numeric output percentiles, but their ranges miss more often under distribution shift.

related_findings.title: Training explicitly for future information
related_findings.summary: Training objectives that target future tokens or insert subgoals for later steps make future tokens easier to identify from model states and improve some task results. Gains vary with model size, architecture and task.

examples.headline: Fine-tuning with future intermediate goals improves graph-task accuracy; gains vary across models and graph structures.
Extra multi-token training goals improve future-token readout, usually worsen next-token readout, and improve held-out Countdown accuracy.
Multi-token training improves small-model induction and polynomial arithmetic; extra token predictors (heads) accelerate code generation.

related_findings.title: Unstated intermediate computation within a forward pass
related_findings.summary: Models represent unstated concepts linking reasoning steps and intermediate arithmetic results within one forward pass. Interventions affect these computations, though ranking changes involving the linking concepts do not establish changes in generated answers.

examples.headline: Mid-layer states reveal unstated concepts linking reasoning steps; replacing their activation directions shifts answer rankings.
Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct represents intermediate arithmetic results; disabling attention heads weakens representations of both intermediate and final results.
Replacing Texas features with California features changes Claude 3.5 Haiku’s answer from Austin to Sacramento.

related_findings.title: State information and move preferences across layers
related_findings.summary: Navigation interventions reveal state information distributed across layers, while chess move preferences continue changing in late layers. These findings concern keeping track of the current state and refining action choices; they do not establish that models look ahead.

examples.headline: Replacing one layer’s state information leaves navigation moves unchanged; effective replacement across all layers changes them.
Leela T82, a chess network, reorders candidate moves through late layers, sometimes dropping correct puzzle moves.
Leela selects the unique winning first move on slightly more than half the composition puzzles.

related_findings.title: Agents with explicit plans
related_findings.summary: Explicit rollouts make agents’ future actions and events more predictable, and trained planning tokens improve task performance. An action-plan matrix with a learned commitment schedule also produces extended actions and structured replanning.

examples.headline: Built-in rollouts (simulations) make MuZero and Thinker’s future actions and events much more predictable.
Disabling trained Planning Tokens lowers performance across tested environments, especially on long-horizon Kitchen-Partial.
An action-plan matrix (action table) learns multi-step actions, triggering maze replanning at corners and junctions.

related_findings.title: Post-training strengthens commitment to response patterns
related_findings.summary: Post-training is linked to more repeated text and stronger commitment to a topic. One study interprets instruction tuning as improving the choice among plans rather than creating planning ability.

examples.headline: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct concentrates on fewer topics, and conflicting topic prefills increase its body entropy.
RLHF generations share longer repeated spans and show greater predictability of their own outputs.
Base-model success patterns suggest instruction tuning refines plan selection rather than creating planning ability.

related_findings.title: Computation beyond visible reasoning text
related_findings.summary: Results from cutting reasoning traces short and using filler with no meaningful content suggest that useful computation can occur outside explicit reasoning text. Outcomes vary with task, model and language, and scores from shortened traces do not measure accuracy with no reasoning trace.

examples.headline: Shortening reasoning traces yields varied results across models, tasks and languages; Nemotron often answers correctly early.
Filler after the question improves accuracy across tasks and models, with exceptions.

related_findings.title: Recent context guides decisions
related_findings.summary: The analyses highlight goal-related text, recent history and nearby preceding tokens as sources of information relevant to decisions. Attention also stays local to paragraphs, though representations within and across paragraphs become harder to distinguish in later layers.

examples.headline: The last token attends mainly to goal-related text and recent history, with recent steps mattering most.
An 8-layer model concentrates information about next-token choices in late layers and recent input tokens.
Attention stays within paragraphs, but similarities between attention outputs distinguish paragraphs less in later layers.

related_findings.title: Why retain information beyond immediate prediction?
related_findings.summary: Hidden states can retain distinctions that do not matter for predicting the next token. The studies offer different explanations: saving information for later positions, or reusing the same computational circuits at multiple positions.

examples.headline: Combining residual-stream signals preserves differences in model beliefs unseen in next-token probabilities, potentially helping later predictions.
Shared training signals teach OthelloGPT features irrelevant to next-token prediction, independently of pre-caching (storing for later).

reading_list.why: Introduces the Claude rhyme intervention and intermediate-feature swap through concrete examples, with limited quantitative evidence.
Compares rhyme probing, patching and steering across model families, exposing model-dependent effects and general-text prediction limits.
Tests rhyme steering across open models and contrasts it with weak answer-number steering, with code and controls.

known_gaps.summary: The main gaps concern independent replication, verified quantitative evidence, general-text prediction and causal tests separating future plans from input conditioning or shared computation.
items: The original Claude rhyme evidence comes from one couplet, without aggregate success rates, uncertainty estimates or a detailed control protocol. Generalization across prompts, simultaneous candidate words and other frontier models remains untested.

Predicting exact tokens two to four positions ahead in general text has not been replicated beyond GPT-J in comparisons with unigram or bigram baselines, which use individual token or token-pair frequencies. Results from constrained contexts do not fill this gap.

Interventions at the last input rhyme word may alter a future plan or simply change how the model uses that word as context. Testing whether patching—replacing internal activity with activity from another example—changes the intermediate words would help distinguish these explanations.

Independent replication within the same model and task remains uncertain, partly because it is unresolved whether studies share authors. Agreement across rhyme, general text and graph tasks does not establish replication within each setting.

Key numerical results for rhyme patching, steering and probing still need verification against the source tables. Some newline-steering evidence is reported only in prose, limiting quantitative comparison.

Information not needed to predict the next token may help predict later tokens, or may arise because the same circuit is reused for different computations. Conflicting results from myopic training, which blocks learning from how internal features help later predictions, still lack a quantitative independent replication.

Editing intermediate “bridge” concepts changes how the model ranks possible answers, but whether it changes generated answers remains unestablished. Evidence for answers being present before visible reasoning also depends on model and language, and scores from cutting reasoning short do not measure accuracy with no visible reasoning at all.
